svg.text: Budgie image input: 12-layer vision tower, width 768, one token per 32 × 32 px
resized to whole 32-px tokens, 64–4,096 tokens in all
widths 3 → 64 → 128 → 256 → 768: one vector per 16 × 16 px patch
patches of all images packed: no padding
QK-norm · 2-D RoPE (half the dims by row, half by column) · 8 heads × 128
Q and K/V each read a 3×3 depthwise conv over the image's patch grid
SiLU / centred dSiLU / SiLU, as in the text model
masked training (keep=): only kept patches run, convs see zeros
each 2×2 square of patch outputs → one 3072-wide vector
the <|image|> embeddings are replaced by the projected vectors,
row-major; nothing in the span is ever predicted
top-16 blocks by compressed score, exactly
every 4×4 block as one pooled key
Up to 1,536 patches the global layers use plain full attention.
How the Budgie 1 tower is trained
1–3 Alone, on the CPU: masked autoencoder
sees 25% of the patches, a small decoder rebuilds the rest
4a Joins the text model: projector only
text model and tower frozen; captions and page text,
images 20% of tokens at 2k → 5% at 256k; budget
6% high-quality image data; long agent runs at 256k
